from.place: The algebraically closed reduction in the proof: over an algebraically closed field, if a fibre had positive dimension it would contain a proper curve, contradicting positivity of the restriction of the symmetric ample module.

title: Multiplication by positive n is locally quasi-finite over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field, let $A$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety] over $K$, and let $n\geq1$. Then the multiplication morphism $[n]:A\to A$ of [def-sc-mult-n] is locally quasi-finite.

source.place: Step 1, the paragraph beginning ‘By [sk-prop-av-symmetric-ample] there is an ample N’

proof.text: Let f = [n]. By [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open], the quasi-finite locus is open and its restriction is locally quasi-finite; hence f is locally quasi-finite exactly when this locus is all of A. If it were proper, properness of A from [def-sc-abelian-variety] and the algebraically closed finite-type hypothesis give a closed point x outside it. Put y = f(x).

source.place: Step 1, the paragraph beginning ‘By [sk-prop-av-symmetric-ample] there is an ample N’

proof.text: The fibre F over y is locally Noetherian because f is locally of finite type, and x is not isolated in F: the quasi-finite-at-x criterion says that {x} is not open in the fibre. A locally Noetherian scheme with a non-open singleton at x has dimension at least one. The fibre is a closed subscheme of the proper finite-type scheme A, so its dimension is finite. Thus 1 ≤ topologicalKrullDim F and topologicalKrullDim F ≠ ⊤.

source.place: Step 1, the sentence ‘The fibre F of [n] over the closed point y ... has positive (and finite) dimension’

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-mult-n-dim-one-closed-subscheme] to obtain a closed immersion i : C → F with topologicalKrullDim C = 1. Since x is a closed point of the finite-type K-scheme A and f is a K-morphism of finite type K-schemes, y = f(x) is a closed point with residue field K (K algebraically closed), so F is a closed subscheme of A and the composite j : C → A is a closed immersion. Hence C is a closed subscheme of the proper, separated, finite-type K-scheme A from [def-sc-abelian-variety], so C is a proper curve over K of dimension one in the sense of [def-sc-curves]. By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective], A carries an ample invertible module L, and by [lem-sc-ample-tensor] N = L ⊗ [-1]^*L is ample with [-1]^*N ≅ N. A closed immersion is an affine morphism, so by [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] j^*N is ample on C (for the proper K-schemes A and C this is the notion of [def-sc-ample], which that definition identifies with the absolute one, Stacks Tag 01Q3).

source.place: Step 1, the sentence ‘contains a proper curve C of dimension one’

proof.text: Since C maps into the fibre over y, f∘j factors through the residue-field point y, so the pullback to C of any invertible module from y is trivial. The symmetry of N and [lem-sc-mult-n-pullback] give f^*N ≅ N^{⊗ n²}; pulling this isomorphism back along j and using the factorization gives (j^*N)^{⊗ n²} ≅ O_C. By [lem-sc-ample-positive-degree], deg(j^*N)>0, while tensor powers multiply degree by n² and O_C has degree zero. Since n≥1, n²>0, contradiction. Thus the quasi-finite locus is all of A.

source.place: Step 1, the final sentence beginning ‘On C the map [n] factors through Spec κ(y)’
